items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to contracts for the transportation of school children
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5618

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the education law, in relation to
contracts for the transportation of school children

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one of this bill contains legislative findings.

Section two of this bill amends paragraph a of subdivision 14 of
section 305 of the Education Law to require the New York City
Department of Education (NYC DOE) to include in its solicitations for
contracts for school bus transportation for children in grades
kindergarten through 12 ("school bus contracts") provisions for the
retention or preference in hiring and the preservation of wages,
health, welfare and retirement benefits and seniority of employees who
perform or performed work for employers party to such contracts, in
connection with such contracts.

Section three amends subdivision 14 of section 305 of the Education
Law by adding a new paragraph g, which would authorize NYC DOE to seek
to amend school bus contracts to include provisions for the retention
or preference in hiring and the preservation of wages, health, welfare
and retirement benefits and seniority of employees who perform or
performed work for employers party to such contracts, in connection
with such contracts.

Section four would include a separability clause.

Section five would require that this bill take effect immediately.

REASONS FOR SUPPORT:

For three decades beginning in 1979, following a school bus strike,
NYC DOE's school bus contracts included employee protection provisions
(EPPs) requiring school transportation contractors, among other
things, to give priority in hiring to employees who became unemployed
because of their employers' loss of NYC DOE bus contract work and to
pay such employees the same wages and benefits they had received prior
to becoming unemployed.

Following the 2011 decision by the New York State Court of Appeals in
L&M Bus Corp., et al., v. the New York City Department of Education,
et al., NYC DOE did not include EPPs or similar provisions in
solicitations for its school bus contracts, which had included such
provisions for over 30 years. After the issuance of the first such
post-L&M solicitation, there was a school bus strike in January and
February of 2013.

This proposal would require NYC DOE to include provisions relating to
the retention or preference in hiring, the preservation of wages,
health, welfare and retirement benefits, and seniority of employees
who perform or performed work for employers party to NYC DOE's school
bus contracts in solicitations for such contracts.

In addition, this proposal would authorize NYC DOE to seek to amend
previously executed school bus contracts to include in such contracts


provisions relating to the retention or preference in hiring, the
preservation of wages, health, welfare and retirement benefits, and
seniority, in connection with such contracts.

This proposal will ensure that NYC DOE's future school bus contracts
will include provisions designed to avoid service disruption and
pension withdrawal liability claims, while protecting the experienced
school bus contract workforce from drastic wage and benefit reductions
and facilitating the retention of an experienced workforce. It will
also enable NYC DOE to seek to amend existing contracts that do not
include such provisions to include them.

Accordingly, the Mayor urges the earliest possible favorable
consideration of this proposal by the Legislature.
